title: Replication package: Screening beats ranking — the value of five copy-trading decisions on a perpetual futures exchange
description:
Code, data and run records for the paper Screening beats ranking: the value of five copy-trading decisions on a perpetual futures exchange.

A copy-trading investor makes five choices: whom to admit as a candidate, how to rank the admitted, how many to hold, what to do when one of them stops, and how much capital each one gets. The package measures what each is worth on a panel of 1,928 Hyperliquid accounts drawn from a public snapshot of 47,195 addresses, net of cost and over a grid of cost levels. The sampling frame is deliberately not a league table: 47.4% of the accounts drawn lost money over their lifetime.

Contents: the pipeline (one file per step), the JSON run record each step writes, the macro file the manuscript reads, and the inputs — the collected panel and two snapshots of the venue's public address list, as gzipped archives. Every number printed in the manuscript is generated from the run records; a number typed into the LaTeX by hand fails the build.

All data are public, pseudonymous, on-chain records. Accounts appear only under the addresses the venue itself publishes.
